key_insight: FL4N represents dynamic 3D scenes in a unified latent space rather than with explicit 4D primitives. The paper introduces this as the first feed-forward latent model for generating views across both camera positions and time.
problem_solved: Reconstructing a moving scene from monocular input requires understanding both 3D structure and motion. Existing feed-forward methods based on explicit 4D Gaussians can produce temporal inconsistencies and severe rendering artifacts.
method: Use a feed-forward model for 4D novel view synthesis from monocular input.
Encode a 4D scene prior into a unified latent representation instead of explicit 4D primitives.
Use the latent scene representation to support rendering across viewpoints and timestamps; further architectural details are unavailable in the provided abstract excerpt.
impact: FL4N offers practitioners an alternative to explicit Gaussian-based representations for dynamic-scene rendering, targeting more coherent results across time. The provided excerpt does not include quantitative results or verified performance gains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular input → unified 4D latent representation → views at different positions and times.

paper_title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Eunbeen Hong, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jooho Son, Hyunah Ko
